text: Most dashboards have a quiet flaw.
When they can't see something, they show green anyway.
Argus is my control room, and it does the opposite.
On every sweep it reads each source: the clouds, the address book, the code host, the server.
If one fails, Argus keeps its last good data and marks it stale.
Then twenty-three rules run against what came back.
Each rule is one file, with its reason and its exceptions written down.
It can break, and name exactly what broke it.
It can be excepted, on purpose, with a reason.
Or it can say it could not check.
Could not check never counts as a pass.
About three thousand tests hold that line.
